# Brief — OSTI-3364673

**What:** Independent replication of the central classification theorem in Kokcu, Wiersema, Kemper, Bakalov (2024) — "Classification of dynamical Lie algebras generated by spin interactions on undirected graphs" (arXiv:2409.19797, DOI 10.1063/5.0283277) — by numerically computing DLA (nested-commutator) closures for the 12 generator families (a_0, a_2, a_4, a_6, a_7, a_14, a_16, a_20, a_22, b_0, b_1, b_3) on a battery of graphs (K_n for n=3,4,5; K_{l,m} for (l,m) ∈ {(1,3),(2,3),(2,2),(3,3),(1,4),(1,5)}; a triangle-plus-pendant; an H-shaped bipartite graph on 6 vertices), and comparing the resulting dimensions to the paper's Theorem I.1 predictions.

**Why:** The theorem is the paper's main claim. Being an all-numerical, all-symbolic combinatorial statement (Lie algebra dimensions as closed-form expressions in n, l, m and BP/NBP), it is directly checkable by nested-commutator closure with no external data required. Two fully independent DLA implementations — a bit-symplectic Pauli tracker and an explicit 2^n×2^n matrix commutator+SVD-independence tracker — were coded from scratch and cross-checked. Result: **101/105 = 96.2 %** of predicted dimensions matched exactly, but a single branch (a_14 on bipartite graphs with both partition sizes l,m odd) disagrees consistently across 4 distinct graphs — numerical dim = 2·dim sp(2^{n-1}) whereas the paper states 2·dim sp(2^{n-2}) — pointing to a probable off-by-one exponent typo in Theorem I.1's a_14 BP-odd-odd branch. Verdict: **PARTIAL**.
